notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text identifies Perceived intent motivates people to magnify observed harms, Daniel L Ames and Susan T Fiske, PNAS 112(12):3599–3605 (2015), DOI 10.1073/pnas.1501592112; PMC4378403 full primary research article text, including results, Materials and Methods, references, and supplementary-material links. Not an abstract-only or secondary report. No PDF supplied; HTML-derived canonical text has no page boundaries, so supplied p.3 cannot be independently mapped to a test. No network/acquisition used. Target ambiguity: study_o is only "2" and description is source-wide (damage/cost assessment, policy priorities, blame motivation). The paper separately labels a Preliminary Experiment, Experiment 1, and Experiment 2. Cannot equate study 2 to either the second experiment overall or the explicitly named Experiment 2. Even Experiment 2 reports several distinct outcomes and tests. No target chosen by row order or numeric matching. Candidates: Preliminary Experiment reports unintentional harm versus ground truth t(117)=0.59, P=0.55; intentional harm versus ground truth t(130)=2.32, P=0.02, d=0.20; intentional versus unintentional harm Welch t(212.22)=1.67, P=0.097. Recruitment/completion counts there do not directly establish target-specific analytic N. Experiment 1 choice: printed chi-square(1)=6.7, P=0.009 for blame-task selection; overall chi-square(4)=11.4, P=0.02; collapsed control-versus-blame chi-square(1)=8.2, P=0.004. Methods explicitly retain all 201 participants, including seven manipulation-check failures; 201 is candidate analytic participant N for Experiment 1 only, not an assigned positive value. Experiment 2 effort: raw clicks t(67.59)=6.0, P=8.7 × 10^−8; log clicks t(114.28)=8.1, P=6.3 × 10^−13; time t(84.12)=3.4, P=.001; rate t(84.85)=7.4, P=1.0 × 10^−10. Response-elasticity mixed ANOVA: intent F(1,101)=60.76, P=4.5 × 10^−12, partial eta-squared=0.374; schedule F(2.8,40.2)=63.96, P=2.5 × 10^−30, partial eta-squared=0.362; interaction F(2.8,300.89)=15.89, P=4 × 10^−9, partial eta-squared=0.129. These are printed candidates only; named effect sizes do not replace requested test statistics. Experiment 2 methods give 120 recruited, 121 data rows, one no-data row and three excluded high-click outliers; four manipulation-check failures retained. Time/rate analyses additionally include only participants clicking at least once, without explicit final subgroup counts here. No N calculated by subtraction or df. No conversion performed. Unassigned replication/success fields are placeholders.
